links.outcome: Response accuracy and understandability differences between patient-role and orthodontist-role prompts
links.effect: Claude 3 Opus (p = 0.001) and Gemini 2.5 (p = 0.023) had higher accuracy in orthodontist role; patient-role responses significantly more understandable than orthodontist-role responses (p < 0.05).
links.quote: Significant chatbot-specific role-based differences were observed, with Claude 3 Opus (p = 0.001) and Gemini 2.5 (p = 0.023) showing higher accuracy in the orthodontist role.

links.outcome: Internal consistency of chatbot responses across scenarios (Cronbach's alpha)
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o (α = 0.862) and Gemini 2.5 (α = 0.815) showed high internal consistency.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o (α = 0.862) and Gemini 2.5 (α = 0.815) showed high internal consistency.

unlisted_practices: Framing of chatbot responses to patient-role prompts (reassuring tone, temporary self-care emphasis) may alter perceived urgency

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the effect of a prompt guardrail/design choice (role-based prompting: patient role vs. orthodontist role) on LLM accuracy, readability, understandability, and urgency communication across simulated orthodontic emergency scenarios.
